source.original_title: 06/10/2026 - Carlos Baston x Andrew Musial KFS
source.display_title: 06/10/2026 - Carlos Baston x Andrew Musial KFS  — Lost

setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: Okay, I spoke with Kim. You spoke with him a few days ago, yeah?

prospect.name: Carlos Baston
prospect.location: On the road; taking the call from Orlando, Florida, USA
prospect.occupation: Long-haul truck driver (approx. 18 months in, targeting 2 years); previously a software engineer
prospect.training_background: Trained his whole life, played one year of school football; keeps dumbbells and resistance bands in the truck; started kettlebells about one week before the call, 20-30 minutes each morning at truck stops plus short sets every 2-3 hours; deep biohacking routine (red light, TENS, yoga nidra, tapping, salt/ACV/creatine water, 80% fat carnivore-style diet, cooks in the cab)
prospect.medical: Became diabetic at 240 lb when younger and lost weight because of it (now 180 lb); shoulder mobility problem for the last six months after over-training in the gym - 'this arm here is being weaker... sometimes it kind of just bothers me'

signals: Explicitly self-sufficient - 'I can get the results myself', 'I'm very resourceful'
Already learning technique from free video; wants a shortcut, not supervision
Balked at a $200/mo product and asked for a first-month discount - price-anchored well below the offer
Proposed label if a better one is wanted: 'the_self_coached_practitioner' - as fit and disciplined as an optimizer but with none of the discretionary income

goals.text: Gain about 10 pounds of muscle in six months, focused on legs and glutes
Fix kettlebell form and get a structured routine rather than random workouts
Move toward longevity and flexibility rather than the bulk-and-shred cycling that made him diabetic

pains.text: Lost most of his muscle since starting truck driving; legs and glutes are the weak point
No technique knowledge - was snatching the bell and letting it drop onto his forearm
Shoulder mobility restricted for six months after over-loading in the gym
Training environment is a truck cab and truck stops; sits all day

objections.raw_quote: Going to box a month seems kind of expensive for just workout programs, I guess on video, but I don't know. I've never done anything like this, so...
objections.rep_response: Shared his screen and walked the Skool classroom, movement library, nutrition module and monthly workout blocks instead of answering the value question.

objections.raw_quote: I got a question, is there a, can I give you a discount on the Primal University to try it out for the first month, or is that not possible?
objections.rep_response: Declined flatly - 'No, there's no discounts, unfortunately.'

evidence: Rep disqualified him from the $6,000 coaching programme before presenting it - 'from what you've told me, you don't really... You that profile... I'd actually be doing you a disservice, putting you on this kind of program'
Prospect asked to buy the coaching anyway - 'what if I had the money and still wanted to do it, you know, to get coaching' - and the rep still steered him to the self-serve product
Ended with 'I'll send you over the email, all the info about the Primal University' and 'I'll take a look at it' - no commitment on either product
Confirmed lost in the 2026-06-10 team meeting: 'it turned out like $200 is a lot for him. So I saved myself 30 minutes.'
outcome.next_step: Rep to email Primal University details; no follow-up call booked.

notable.note: The clean disqualification is genuinely good conduct and the rep held price when asked for a discount. Two things sit against it. First, the prospect explicitly asked to buy the $6,000 coaching for form feedback and a leg-focused programme and was talked out of it - demand existed and was declined on the rep's read of the prospect's wallet, not his fit. Second, a type 2 diabetes history and a six-month shoulder impairment were disclosed and then steered into an unsupervised self-paced kettlebell and steel-mace product with no clinician question at all.

quality.notes: Large blocks invert - the rep's injury question at 00:02:00 and his entire Primal University pitch at 00:23:00-00:24:30 are labelled to the prospect, and the prospect's answers appear under the rep. Roles read from content. Rep's Fathom label reads 'Andrew Jin (Primal Instinct)' against a title and folder naming Andrew Musial. Call also interrupted by a dispatch phone call at 00:03:56.
